title: The pod has watched Sisay activate once: fetch Najeela, or the card that makes Najeela unanswerable later?

board.you: Turn 8, your precombat main, 34 life, never attacked. Battlefield: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain, Katilda, Dawnhart Prime (green/white), Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy (green/blue), Reki, the History of Kamigawa (green — fetched last turn, in full view of the table), Faeburrow Elder, and nine lands including Command Tower, City of Brass and Sacred Foundry. Colours among your other legendary permanents: green, white, blue — three — so Sisay is a 5/5 and 28 of the 33 fetchable legends are legal (everything at mana value 4 or less; Jodah, Jegantha, Kenrith, Samut and Surrak at mana value 5 still need a fourth colour). You can pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} exactly once: Faeburrow Elder gives {G}{W}{U} (only the colours among your permanents), City of Brass gives {B}, Sacred Foundry gives {R}. Four lands remain open after the activation.
board.table: Player 2 (Dimir control, 31 life) has held exactly two blue sources open at every end step for three turns and cast nothing — assume a counterspell and possibly a second piece of interaction (stated archetypal assumption). Player 3 (Boros aggro, 22 life) has four creatures and an anthem and has attacked Player 4 for two turns running. Player 4 (Golgari midrange) is at 18 and visibly dying to it. Everyone at the table watched Sisay fetch Reki last turn, and this is a bracket 4 pod: the deck's four Game Changers (Drannith Magistrate, Fierce Guardianship, Rhystic Study, Seedborn Muse) and its four two-card infinites were on the table in the pregame conversation. Nobody here believes you are a fair legends deck.

scenario.question: Najeela, the Blade-Blossom is mana value 3 and shares Sisay's exact {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation cost — she is both this deck's finisher candidate and the single card that tells the table to kill you next. Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar is also mana value 3 and reads 'Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn'. Shalai, Voice of Plenty is 4. Thalia, Heretic Cathar is 3 and slows the seat that is actually killing people. Which do you take first?

branches.line: Pay the five pips, put Najeela onto the battlefield. She is a 3/2 with no haste, so she cannot attack this turn, and her ability is 'Activate only during combat' at a second full {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — which this board can pay exactly once per turn. Concretely: she makes 1/1 Warrior tokens when Warriors attack and does nothing else until the mana doubles.
branches.signals: Maximum. At a bracket 4 table, Najeela next to a five-colour mana base is read as 'they have it', full stop — and your four two-card infinites in the bracket report all route through her. You have announced the kill a turn or more before you can attempt it.
branches.coalition_risk: High, immediate, and paid early. The Dimir player's held card gets repointed at you, Boros reconsiders which seat to attack, and Player 4 trades their removal into your board instead of stabilising against the aggro deck. You just did the coalition's threat assessment for it.
branches.coaching: This is the deflection budget spent on the turn the card impresses instead of the turn it wins, and two problems compound. Mana first: Najeela's untap-all-attackers ability wants the same five pips Sisay just spent, so on this board she is a 3/2 that does nothing for a full turn cycle. Second — and this shapes how you read this whole issue — exactly one of the four Najeela lines has a checker-passed resolution in this manual, Najeela plus Derevi, and its verdict is that the loop is real and lethal but NOT the two-card infinite the combo data advertises, because each iteration owes another five coloured pips. The other three Najeela lines are candidates from the combo data, not verified kills. So this fetch buys the archenemy label at the price of a win you cannot demonstrate this turn. Now flip the asymmetry to your side: the table treats those lines as verified whether or not they are, which makes Najeela worth more to you in the library than on the battlefield. That is the luxury a repeatable battlefield tutor buys you and almost no other deck gets. You never need to hold your finisher — you need the mana to fetch and fire it in one turn.

citations.quote: Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress.

Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail, and sequence the scariest piece last so the deflection budget (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) lasts until the turn you take it.

branches.line: Pay the five pips, put Kutzil onto the battlefield — a 3/3 for effectively {1}{G}{W} whose first line is 'Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn'. From your next untap step, the Dimir player's counterspell, every instant-speed removal spell at the table and every shrink-the-ladder response is dead during your turn — the only turn Sisay activates and the only turn Najeela could ever be activated. Bonus: Sisay's base power is 2 and she is a 5/5, a creature 'with power greater than its base power', so Kutzil's second ability turns her connections into cards.
branches.signals: A three-mana 3/3 Cat reads as a fair value creature and a blocker. Tables do not price a hatebear the way they price a combo piece, and the Boros player may even read it as a wall you fetched because you are scared of them. That is exactly the fetch to make while the spotlight is on somebody else.
branches.coalition_risk: Low. Nothing about this board re-ranks you above a Boros deck putting Player 4 to 18.
branches.coaching: The scary target and the correct target differ by one step of ordering: fetch the card that makes the scary card unanswerable, then fetch the scary card on the turn you can use it. Kutzil converts your entire turn into an uninterruptible window, and this deck needs that more than most — all six counterspells and both free protection instants are non-legendary and invisible to Sisay, so protection-on-the-stack must be drawn while protection-by-permanent is fetched on demand. Two honest limits, so you are never surprised. Kutzil stops SPELLS, not activated abilities: a sacrifice outlet, a Pithing Needle, an opposing activated removal ability all still function on your turn — and Grand Abolisher, which covers both halves, is one of the 26 cards Sisay can never find. And Kutzil does nothing on other players' turns, which inverts the usual commit-at-the-end-step advice: once he is on board, your own main phase is the safest priority window at the table. Activate there.

Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress.

branches.line: Pay the five pips for a 3/4 flier at mana value 4 who gives you, your planeswalkers and every OTHER creature you control hexproof. Sisay, Katilda, Kinnan and Reki all become untargetable. So does your face, which turns off burn and targeted drain from the Boros seat.
branches.signals: Reads as 'my commander is my deck and I know it'. Experienced tables answer that with sweepers and edicts rather than spot removal, and start counting your recast tax.
branches.coalition_risk: Medium. Insurance is a fair-looking fetch, but it confirms the diagnosis — you have told the table which single permanent to route around.
branches.coaching: Right fetch, wrong table. Price insurance against the interaction this specific pod actually runs, and the read here says counterspell, not removal — the Dimir player has held exactly two blue at every end step for three turns. Hexproof does nothing about a counterspell. And note the mirror fact: a counterspell does nothing about Sisay's activation either, because an activated ability is not a spell. Shalai's real job here is defending against the Golgari and Boros seats' targeted removal, which is not what threatens you at 34 life and untouched. So schedule her instead of skipping her: take Shalai the moment the shrink attack is shown, the moment a colour rung eats spot removal, or pre-emptively at a removal-heavy pod. And remember what she does not cover — she does not protect herself, and she does nothing against Toxic Deluge-style -X/-X, sweepers or edicts, the effects that collapse the ladder from power 5 back to power 2, where only three cards in the deck are legal fetches and this deck runs zero legendary lands to soften the landing.

citations.quote: When the engine routes through your commander, protection is insurance priced against the recast tax: each return trip to the command zone adds {2} per prior command-zone cast (Miljkovac) — and, the bigger price, a tempo turn spent re-casting instead of advancing.

branches.choice: Fetch Thalia, Heretic Cathar and keep the aggro deck pointed elsewhere
branches.line: A 3/2 first-striker at mana value 3 whose static reads 'Creatures and nonbasic lands your opponents control enter tapped'. It taxes every new Boros threat by a turn, taxes the Golgari rebuild, and slows the Simic-style land-and-body seats that rely on untapped nonbasics.
branches.signals: Unambiguously reads as hate aimed at the Boros player, and buys real goodwill from Player 4 at 18 life. It is also the fetch that most convincingly sells 'I am a fair legends deck'.
branches.coalition_risk: Lowest of the four — it actively moves the table's attention away from you, at the price of a turn spent on somebody else's problem.
branches.coaching: The seat-relative read is real: Boros is the clock, Player 4 is the one dying, and a good threat-assessment habit reaches here. Now run the answer economy honestly. Thalia does not touch the four creatures already on the battlefield — she taxes the next ones. At 34 life, untouched, with the aggro deck's attention on a player at 18, the aggression is not yet pointed at you, and answering a threat somebody else was about to answer for you is one of the classic ways to lose a game of Commander from the safest seat at the table. Pocket this fetch for the turn Boros turns the corner and swings at you, or the turn Player 4 dies and you inherit the clock. That is the moment this whole scenario changes.

citations.quote: The classic leaks: killing the scariest creature instead of the one that beats you, spending removal on sight instead of at the last profitable moment, and answering a threat someone else was about to answer for you.

recommendation.rationale: The correct fetch sits one step earlier in the chain than the scary one. Kutzil costs the same mana value as Najeela, reads as a fair 3/3, and makes every future turn of yours a window in which the Dimir player's held counterspell and the whole table's instant-speed removal are simply illegal — the one thing this deck cannot buy any other way, since all six of its counterspells and both free protection instants are non-legendary and unfetchable. Najeela gains nothing from arriving early: she costs a second full {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} you cannot pay this turn, and the one Najeela line this issue verifies — the Derevi combat loop — is precisely the one that proves the pair generates no mana of its own, so the pips must arrive every single combat. Fetching her now spends the deflection budget on a threat you cannot fire. She is a permanent in your library and Sisay is repeatable: take her on the turn the mana doubles and the window is already shut. Fetch the enabler, keep the tell in the library, and let the Boros player stay the table's problem.
